title: Halbeisen-style min_σ of the slack-weight functional yields a closure inequality beyond lowerDenom and (L,o)
statement: The unfolded weights α_i(w)=2^i 3^{#O(w[i+1:])} and S=sum α, or the cyclic-shift optimum M_{L,o}=max_w min_σ S(w), give a closure inequality that excludes a leftover-shaped necklace which (L,o), lowerDenom, and run-type finance do not already exclude.
counterexamples: lowerDenom(w)=4^{S(w)} on all 511 itineraries of length ≤8, so the n-independent functional is the existing size bound cycle_pow_le_lowerDenom
OE and EO have S=3 and S=5 but are rotations; min_σ S is a necklace invariant, not a new pair-level obstruction
Every OO-prefix with fixed (L,o) shares the leading weights (3^{o-1}, 2·3^{o-2}). Cyclic-shift optimization does not apply to the CycleMin start
17 expanding (L,o) pairs through length 8: 9 have several S values and 3 have several min_σ S values; new_necklace_kills=0
At L=19 the mechanical OOE/OE word has S=2816889 against bunched S=1047537, so the finance-relevant shape has the weaker 4^{S/g} bound
mathematical_domain: Juggler cycle finance / cyclic word functionals
notes: The Collatz methodology was the right import; the affine φ(s) miracle does not survive floor powers. No Paper A edit, no ledger row, no Lean. Not a halt theorem.
tested_range: identity n≤24, k≤4 (92 orbits); denom and necklace census k≤8 (511 words, 17 expanding pairs); shaped words at L=5,8,11,19
